entries.title: Luke 20:1
segments: On one of these days, when Jesus was teaching the people in the Temple Courts and telling the Good News, the Chief Priests and the Teachers of the Law, joined by the Councillors, confronted him,

entries.title: Luke 20:2
segments: And addressing him, said: "Tell us what authority you have to do these things. Who is it that has given you this authority?"

entries.title: Luke 20:3
segments: "I, too," said Jesus in reply, "will ask you one question. Give me an answer to it.

entries.title: Luke 20:4
segments: It is about John's baptism--was it of divine or of human origin?"

entries.title: Luke 20:5
segments: But they began arguing together: "If we say 'divine,' he will say 'Why did not you believe him?'

entries.title: Luke 20:6
segments: But, if we say 'human,' the people will all stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a Prophet."

entries.title: Luke 20:7
segments: So they answered that they did not know its origin.

entries.title: Luke 20:8
segments: "Then I," said Jesus, "refuse to tell you what authority I have to do these things."

entries.title: Luke 20:9
segments: But Jesus began to tell the people this parable--"A man once planted a vineyard, and then let it out to tenants, and went abroad for a long while.

entries.title: Luke 20:10
segments: At the proper time he sent a servant to the tenants, that they should give him a share of the produce of the vineyard. The tenants, however, beat him and sent him away empty-handed.

entries.title: Luke 20:11
segments: The owner afterwards sent another servant; but the tenants beat and insulted this man too, and sent him away empty-handed.

entries.title: Luke 20:12
segments: He sent a third; but they wounded this man also, and threw him outside.

entries.title: Luke 20:13
segments: 'What shall I do?' said the owner of the vineyard. 'I will send my son, who is very dear to me. Perhaps they will respect him.'

entries.title: Luke 20:14
segments: But, on seeing him, the tenants consulted with one another. 'Here is the heir!' they said. 'Let us kill him, and then the inheritance will become ours.'

entries.title: Luke 20:15
segments: So they threw him outside the vineyard and killed him. Now what will the owner of the vineyard do to them?

entries.title: Luke 20:16
segments: He will come and put those tenants to death, and will let the vineyard to others." "Heaven forbid!" they exclaimed when they heard it.

entries.title: Luke 20:17
segments: But Jesus looked at them and said: "What then is the meaning of this passage?-- 'The very stone which the builders despised has now itself become the corner-stone.'

entries.title: Luke 20:18
segments: Every one who falls on that stone will be dashed to pieces, while any one on whom it falls--it will scatter him as dust."

entries.title: Luke 20:19
segments: After this the Teachers of the Law and the Chief Priest were eager to lay hands on Jesus then and there, but they were afraid of the people; for they saw that it was at them that he had aimed this parable.

entries.title: Luke 20:20
segments: Having watched their opportunity, they afterwards sent some spies, who pretended to be good men, to catch Jesus in the course of conversation, and so enable them to give him up to the Governor's jurisdiction and authority.

entries.title: Luke 20:21
segments: These men asked Jesus a question. They said: "Teacher, we know that you are right in what you say and teach, and that you do not take any account of a man's position, but teach the Way of God honestly;

entries.title: Luke 20:22
segments: Are we right in paying tribute to the Emperor or not?"

entries.title: Luke 20:23
segments: Seeing through their deceitfulness, Jesus said to them:

entries.title: Luke 20:24
segments: "Show me a florin. Whose head and title are on it?"

entries.title: Luke 20:25
segments: "The Emperor's," they said; and Jesus replied: "Well then, pay to the Emperor what belongs to the Emperor, and to God what belongs to God."

entries.title: Luke 20:26
segments: They could not lay hold of this answer before the people; and, in their wonder at his reply, they held their tongues.

entries.title: Luke 20:27
segments: Presently there came up some Sadducees, who maintain that there is no resurrection. Their question was this--

entries.title: Luke 20:28
segments: "Teacher, Moses laid down for us in his writings that-- 'Should a man's married brother die, and should he be childless, the man should take the widow as his wife, and raise up a family for his brother.'

entries.title: Luke 20:29
segments: Well, there were once seven brothers; of whom the eldest, after taking a wife, died childless.

entries.title: Luke 20:30
segments: The second and third brothers both took her as their wife;

entries.title: Luke 20:31
segments: And so, too, did all seven--dying without children.

entries.title: Luke 20:32
segments: The woman herself was the last to die.

entries.title: Luke 20:33
segments: About the woman, then--at the resurrection, whose wife is she to be, all seven brothers having had her as their wife?"

entries.title: Luke 20:34
segments: "The men and women of this world," said Jesus, "marry and are given in marriage;

entries.title: Luke 20:35
segments: But, for those who are thought worthy to attain to that other world and the resurrection from the dead, there is no marrying or being married,

entries.title: Luke 20:36
segments: Nor indeed can they die again, for they are like angels and, having shared in the resurrection, they are God's Sons.

entries.title: Luke 20:37
segments: As to the fact that the dead rise, even Moses indicated that, in the passage about the Bush, when he calls the Lord--'The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.'

entries.title: Luke 20:38
segments: Now he is not God of dead men, but of living. For in his sight all are alive."

entries.title: Luke 20:39
segments: "Well said, Teacher!" exclaimed some of the Teachers of the Law,

entries.title: Luke 20:40
segments: For they did not venture to question him any further.

entries.title: Luke 20:41
segments: But Jesus said to them: "How is it that people say that the Christ is to be David's son?

entries.title: Luke 20:42
segments: For David, in the Book of Psalms, says himself--'The Lord said to my lord: "Sit at my right hand,

entries.title: Luke 20:43
segments: Until I put they enemies as a stool for thy feet."'

entries.title: Luke 20:44
segments: David, then, calls him 'lord,' so how is he David's son?"

entries.title: Luke 20:45
segments: While all the people were listening, Jesus said to the disciples:

entries.title: Luke 20:46
segments: "Be on your guard against the Teachers of the Law, who delight to walk about in long robes, and like to be greeted in the streets with respect, and to have the best seats in the Synagogues, and places of honor at dinner.

entries.title: Luke 20:47
segments: These are the men who rob widows of their houses, and make a pretense of saying long prayers. Their sentence will be all the heavier."
